note.backdrop: Before Tuesday's open the market is waiting: SPY -0.0%, QQQ +0.4%, IWM -0.3%, S&P futures -0.1%, VIX -0.7%; oil +1.1%, the 10-year flat, bitcoin +0.1%. No market-wide flag and no fear flag; this morning the futures line is measured from Monday's close (it moved -0.06% after the close last night), so last night's false market-wide flag is gone. Earlier reports had futures down about 0.3%-0.4% at 5am ET (Invezz, Investing.com). The day's event is Nvidia's third-quarter report after the close, its first under an interim chief: analysts expect revenue near $109 billion against the company's own guidance of $108 billion plus or minus 2%, with data-center revenue near $101.8 billion (TradingKey, Invezz). Anthropic is due to list on Nov 19. October retail sales and import prices are also due (Invezz). Three stocks are outside their 9-in-10 range: one on a trial result, one on results, one on a single thin print.

read.says: By 5:23am ET S&P 500 E-minis were -0.34%; Nvidia slipped 0.4% before its results; CNBC reported Nvidia told customers it would stop selling chips to data-center operators that rent more than half their GPUs to Chinese companies; Intel fell over 3% after Nvidia cut its stake in Intel in a portfolio reshuffle (also Nokia and Synopsys, while adding SpaceX); Home Depot named its finance chief as next chief executive and raised its sales outlook to the top of its range.
Futures about -0.4% before Nvidia's report and retail sales; analysts expect Nvidia revenue of about $109 billion; Nvidia closed Monday at $156.14 (-4.12%).

Nvidia's guidance was $108 billion plus or minus 2% with a 74% gross margin; Visible Alpha expects $109.3 billion and data-center revenue of about $101.8 billion; Anthropic plans to list on Nov 19; Red Cat fell over 30% before the open after withdrawing its 2026 revenue guidance.

Sellas' Phase 3 REGAL trial of its vaccine galinpepimut-S in acute myeloid leukemia met its main goal: 41% lower risk of death (hazard ratio 0.59, two-sided p 0.035), median survival 24.0 months against 14.7 with the best available treatment; it plans to meet the FDA and prepare an application.
Spire lowered its fiscal 2027 adjusted earnings guidance to $5.05-$5.25 a share, introduced fiscal 2028 guidance of $6.10-$6.30, raised its long-term growth target to 6%-8% and its dividend by 4.8%.
Knight-Swift's pre-market trading on the 5-minute chart: three bars, all at $58.40, between 7:00 and 7:17am ET.
Sellas on the 5-minute chart: $7.78 at 4am ET, $30.20 at 8:35am ET, 27 pre-market bars.

singles.beneath: It was worth about $1.5 billion at Monday's close, so the jump adds about $4.4 billion on 27 pre-market bars. The p-value of 0.035 is under 0.05 but not by much; the FDA's view of one trial at that level is the open question (inference). It had $134.7 million of cash at Sept 30 and has sold new shares five times in three years; the mosaic put a share-sale filing within 20 sessions at 7.3% against 0.9% for the usual stock, before this move. That is a chance that a filing comes, not a direction. This is the kind of binary readout the post-mortem's step 4 is about: no probability was written for it before.
singles.cause: Sellas rose 295% before the open after its Phase 3 REGAL trial in acute myeloid leukemia met its main goal: a 41% lower risk of death (hazard ratio 0.59, two-sided p 0.035), median survival 24.0 months against 14.7 with the best available treatment. It plans to meet the FDA about an application.

themes.beneath: The bar: guidance was $108 billion plus or minus 2%, so $105.8-$110.2 billion, with a 74% gross margin; analysts sit near $109 billion (TradingKey). Nvidia has lost about $410 billion of market value since its chief resigned (Investing.com). The desk's open calls from Nov 13, judged Nov 20, are sizes, either way: Nvidia 7.5% or more (chance 0.50), AMD 9% or more (0.42), Dell 9.5% or more (0.40).
themes.cause: After Monday's falls the AI hardware group is slightly higher before the open: Nvidia +1.1%, AMD +2.0%, Broadcom +1.1%, Micron +1.2%, Dell +1.5%, Super Micro +1.7%, CoreWeave +1.6%. Intel is -1.0% on the check (over -3% in an earlier report) after Nvidia cut its stake in Intel in a portfolio reshuffle (Investing.com). CNBC reported, per the same article, that Nvidia told customers it will stop selling chips to data-center operators that rent more than half their GPUs to Chinese companies; I could not find that report itself, so it stands on one summary.
themes.mechanism: Nothing new reached the group overnight except Nvidia's own steps; the moves are small against Monday's falls (Nvidia +1.1% after -4.1%). The report tonight is the event that reaches all of them: Nvidia's data-center revenue is about 93% of the expected total (about $101.8 billion of $109 billion), and its customers' spending is the revenue of everyone else in this group. My inference: what Nvidia says about demand next quarter, and about the five-country license rule, carries more for the group than the quarter just ended.
